question: A 38-year-old man consulted for dyspnea and hemoptysis. Blood tests have creatinine 7 mg / dl, urea 250 mg / dl and anti-MBG (anti-glomerular basement membrane antibodies) positive high titer. A renal biopsy was performed, showing crescents in 75% of the glomeruli, and in the immunofluorescence a linear Ig deposition pattern appeared. Which of the following is the correct answer?

options.opa: It is an Ig A Nephropathy with acute renal failure.
options.opb: The performance of plasmapheresis would be indicated.
options.opd: Mycophenolate mofetil is the initial treatment of choice.
options.ope: Glomerular involvement is caused by the presence of circulating immune complexes.

paths: (antibody positive)-PREDISPOSES->(Diabetes Mellitus, Non-Insulin-Dependent)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(physiological aspects)-PROCESS_OF->(Structure of parenchyma of lung)-LOCATION_OF->(Fluorescent Antibody Technique)

(antibody positive)-PREDISPOSES->(Diabetes Mellitus, Non-Insulin-Dependent)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(physiological aspects)-PROCESS_OF->(Skeletal muscle structure)-LOCATION_OF->(Fluorescent Antibody Technique)

(antibody positive)-PREDISPOSES->(Diabetes Mellitus, Non-Insulin-Dependent)-MANIFESTATION_OF->(physiological aspects)-PROCESS_OF->(Structure of parenchyma of lung)-LOCATION_OF->(Fluorescent Antibody Technique)

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Anti-MBG antibodies positive high titer -> Linear Ig deposition pattern in immunofluorescence -> Suggestive of anti-GBM disease -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Renal biopsy showing crescents in 75% of glomeruli -> Indicative of rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Creatinine 7 mg/dL, urea 250 mg/dL -> Indicate acute renal failure -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Presence of circulating immune complexes -> Glomerular involvement in this case -> 70% confidence. CHAIN: Plasmapheresis indicated for anti-GBM disease with high titers -> 90%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with dyspnea, hemoptysis, positive anti-GBM antibodies with high titers, linear Ig deposition pattern on renal biopsy, and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis indicate a diagnosis of anti-GBM disease. Plasmapheresis is indicated as the initial treatment of choice in this condition to remove circulating antibodies. The presence of circulating immune complexes is not the primary cause of glomerular involvement in this case.
analysis: The patient's presentation with dyspnea, hemoptysis, positive anti-GBM antibodies with high titers, linear Ig deposition pattern on renal biopsy, and rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis strongly suggest a diagnosis of anti-GBM disease. Plasmapheresis is the standard initial treatment to remove circulating antibodies in this condition. The presence of circulating immune complexes is not the primary cause of glomerular involvement in this case.
